blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A service holds `private final String[] regions = {"eu-west", "us-east", "ap-south"}` and exposes `List<String> regions() { return Arrays.asList(regions); }`. A report calls `Collections.shuffle(service.regions())` to visit regions in random order. What does the next caller of `regions()` get?

options.text: The original order, since the list `regions()` returns is a copy of the array
options.says: Arrays.asList copies nothing: the list reads and writes the array it was given

options.text: The shuffled order, since the list `regions()` returns reads and writes the array
options.says: the list is a view of the service's array, so shuffling it rearranges the array every later call sees

options.text: An exception from `shuffle`, since the list `regions()` returns refuses every change
options.says: only changes of size throw; set and sort reach the array, so a reordering goes through

options.text: An exception from `shuffle`, since the list `regions()` returns is checked against the array's order
options.says: nothing checks the order; the list writes straight through to the array

origin.section: Arrays.asList Adapts an Array Without Copying It, So Sorting the List Reorders the Array

questions.stem: A batch job reads UTF-8 partner files with `new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(Files.newInputStream(path)))`. Its tests pass on every developer machine (Java 21). The production container starts the JVM with `-Dfile.encoding=ISO-8859-1`. What does the job make of a customer named `Zoë`?

options.text: It reads `Zoë`, since Java 18 and later decode streams as UTF-8 whatever the JVM is started with
options.says: UTF-8 is only the default's default; a JVM started with another file.encoding uses that charset

options.text: It stops with an error, since the bytes of `ë` are rejected by the charset it decodes with
options.says: the reader built without a decoder replaces or mis-decodes; nothing throws, which is why the broken names get stored

options.text: It stores `ZoÃ«`, since each byte of `ë` is decoded on its own as a character of the JVM's charset
options.says: the one-argument constructor uses the machine's default charset, here Latin-1, which turns each UTF-8 byte into a character of its own

options.text: It stores `Zo�`, since each byte of `ë` that the JVM's charset can't decode becomes U+FFFD
options.says: Latin-1 has a character for every byte, so the bytes are mis-decoded, not replaced

origin.section: InputStreamReader Adapts Bytes to Chars Through a Charset, and the One-Argument Constructor Takes the JVM's Default

questions.stem: An adapter turns a legacy SDK's callback into a `CompletableFuture`; the SDK calls back on its single event thread. A handler calls `adapter.fetch(id).thenApply(doc -> renderPdf(doc))` as soon as `fetch` returns, before the document arrives, and `renderPdf` takes two seconds. What happens to the other fetches while a PDF renders?

options.text: Their answers wait for the rendering, since `renderPdf` runs on the thread that completed the future
options.says: a stage attached before completion runs on the thread that calls complete, here the SDK's only event thread

options.text: Their answers wait for the rendering, since `thenApply` holds the handler's thread until `renderPdf` returns
options.says: thenApply returns a new stage at once; it never blocks the thread that attaches it

options.text: They go on as before, since `renderPdf` runs in the common `ForkJoinPool` the future uses
options.says: only the Async forms run in the common pool; thenApply runs on the completing thread or the caller's

options.text: They go on as before, since `renderPdf` runs on the handler's thread that attached it
options.says: the attaching thread runs the stage only when the future is already complete, which it isn't here

origin.section: Continuations Run on Whichever Thread Completes the Future

questions.stem: A library parses anything that is a `java.io.Reader`. Your data comes from a legacy class `LedgerFile` with `String nextLine()`, and a factory gives you the `LedgerFile` to use. A colleague proposes `class LedgerReader extends LedgerFile implements Reader { ... }`. What happens?

options.text: javac refuses it, since `Reader` is a class and `LedgerReader` already extends one
options.says: Reader is an abstract class, so it can't follow implements, and a class extends only one class; only an object adapter extending Reader works

options.text: javac refuses it, since `LedgerFile` would have to be an interface for this to work
options.says: the target, Reader, is the problem; a class adapter extends the adaptee class and implements a target interface

options.text: It compiles and adapts the factory's `LedgerFile`, since `LedgerReader` inherits its lines
options.says: it doesn't compile; and a class adapter adapts only instances it constructs, never one a factory made

options.text: It compiles and adapts new `LedgerFile`s only, since inheritance works on classes, not objects
options.says: with Reader an abstract class it doesn't compile at all; that limit applies to interface targets

origin.section: Java Has Only Object Adapters When the Target Is a Class

concepts: A receiver that must not see the array's changes, or make its own, gets a copy: new ArrayList<>(...) or List.copyOf(...).
When the target is a class, such as Reader, a class adapter doesn't compile and only an object adapter works; for an interface target a class adapter still adapts only instances it constructs.
A non-async stage attached before the future completes runs on the thread that completes it, here the legacy client's I/O thread; slow work goes to thenApplyAsync with an executor.
